name: Citizenship by Descent

requirements.blocker_text: Born to a Tunisian father OR a Tunisian mother (Article 6, as amended in 2010) -- applies without gender distinction, regardless of where the child is born.

requirement_groups.name: Transitional declaration for adults born before the 2010 reform

requirements.blocker_text: An adult born abroad to a Tunisian mother and a foreign father, before the 2010 reform, may claim nationality by declaration if registered within one year of the amendment -- a closing, historically-bounded window rather than an ongoing route for new cases.

sources.title: ecoi.net (NGO-hosted country-of-origin information repository) -- French text of Tunisia's Code de la nationalité tunisienne: Article 6 (as modified in 2010) grants nationality to a child born to a Tunisian father OR mother without gender distinction; a transitional provision allowed adults born abroad to a Tunisian mother and foreign father before the reform to claim nationality by declaration if registered within one year of the 2010 amendment

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Tunisia). STATUS: DRAFT -- only an NGO-hosted (ecoi.net) copy of the Code was fetchable in this build; Tunisia's own Ministry of Justice hosts an Arabic-language PDF of the Code (justice.gov.tn) that was located via search but not independently translated/verified in this build -- a genuine follow-up opportunity to upgrade this file's sourcing tier, since the primary text does appear to be government-hosted, just not in a form this build could process within the time available. GENUINE POSITIVE FINDING: descent citizenship has been fully gender-neutral since a 2010 reform -- either a Tunisian mother or father transmits citizenship on equal terms, joining Kenya, Pakistan (post-2000), and India (post-1992) as countries in this dataset with a genuinely reformed, equal descent rule. dual_citizenship_allowed set to TRUE -- Tunisia is broadly reported to permit dual nationality with no general renunciation requirement, though this specific point was not independently verified against a primary legal source in this build and should be treated as provisional.
